title: shell_execute arguments
description: The arguments of the browser server's shell_execute tool, which is input.arguments of the mcp_tools policy input when input.server is "browser" and input.tool is "shell_execute". The tool refuses anything that does not match, but a policy is asked BEFORE the tool validates: in a policy every field can be missing or of any type. Exactly one of argv and script. images/browser/test/shell.test.mjs checks that the tool advertises these properties.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, executed directly: no shell, no word splitting, no globbing, no expansion. argv[0] is a name looked up on the server's PATH (which env cannot change) or a path.

script.description: Shell source, run as bash -lc <script>. Opaque to a policy beyond string matching.

cwd.description: Working directory. Absolute and already normalised (no '.', '..', '//' or trailing '/'), an existing directory with no symbolic link anywhere in the path, equal to or inside one of the allowed roots (the user's home, /data, /tmp). Default: the user's home directory ($HOME of the desktop).

env.description: Variables added to the desktop's environment. Refused names: PATH, BASH_ENV, ENV, SHELLOPTS, BASHOPTS, PS4, NODE_OPTIONS, and any name starting with LD_ or BASH_FUNC_. At most 64 variables, 32768 bytes in all.

stdin.description: Written to the command's standard input, which is then closed. Without it standard input is /dev/null.

timeout_ms.description: After this long the command's process group is sent SIGTERM, and SIGKILL two seconds later. In the foreground: default 30000, maximum 600000. With background: true: no default (the command runs until it exits or is killed), maximum 86400000.

max_output_bytes.description: The most bytes kept of stdout, and of stderr (each has its own count). In the background, of output not yet polled.

background.description: Start the command and return {id, pid, started_at} at once; read its output and end it with the shell_process tool.
